[0] Siri AI is a major upgrade for Apple's assistant in iOS 27, and among the many areas, there is one aspect where I noticed it is clearly different from other AI assistants, and it's on the positive side.

[1] The new Siri in iOS 27 does not pretend to be human, unlike all other AI chatbots

[2] I have been using the Siri AI in the iOS 27 beta for nearly two months. So far, it has done everything I expected of it.

[3] The new Siri is far more powerful than its previous version, delivering on its original promise of becoming a truly capable assistant on Apple devices.

[4] However, I have to admit that if you want the most powerful, cutting-edge AI tools, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini may be a better fit for you.

[5] Nevertheless, after using Siri AI and comparing it with these third-party tools, I found one key difference that makes me greatly favor Siri.

[6] Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri does not pretend to be human.

[7] It is not overly verbose, nor does it mimic human-like personalities to subtly get you to build a personal relationship with it.

[8] Siri is helpful, intelligent, and does what you ask it to do. But the way it responds clearly shows that it is just a tool, not a person. It regularly reminds you that it is an AI and may therefore make mistakes. It also does not pretend to flirt with you.

[9] In contrast, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are full of personality, have their own opinions, and display more human-like tendencies, which I find insincere.

[10] I suppose some users will prefer that more 'personalized' approach. But I much prefer AI assistants to do their job and not put on an act.

[11] AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are just tools, not people. I really appreciate that Apple understands this and has designed the new Siri accordingly.

[12] How 'human-like' do you think AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
